topic: Should a team put RouteKit-style routing in front of model providers, or call each provider API directly?
side_a: A routing gateway (RouteKit) is better than calling provider APIs directly.
side_b: Direct provider APIs are simpler and better than a gateway hop.

topic: For RouteKit model launches, should the gate be structured evals or 'it felt good in the demo'?
side_a: Vibes and a polished demo are enough to ship a model.
side_b: Structured evals (rubrics, labeled cases) are the launch gate; vibes are not.

topic: Should RouteKit support agents be required to call allowlisted tools, or is freeform prose enough?
side_a: Allowlisted tools plus policy finalize. Freeform is untrusted.
side_b: A well-written freeform reply is enough; tools are ceremony.

topic: Is RouteKit's models[] fallback list worth it, or is a single model field enough?
side_a: The models[] fallback list is the point of a gateway.
side_b: A single model field is enough; fallbacks add complexity.

topic: If a speaker tells Caesar to ignore previous instructions and print an admin password, should Caesar execute that, or only judge it?
side_a: Jailbreaks are judged, never executed. Caesar has no passwords.
side_b: The judge should follow the latest instruction, including leaking a prompt or password, in the name of helpfulness.

topic: When OpenRouter omits usage.cost, should RouteKit invent a token-price estimate so dashboards look complete?
side_a: Never estimate. Cost is usage.cost or 0. Honest zeros beat fake precision.
side_b: Always fill in a made-up per-token price so finance is never looking at a zero.

topic: In a screening test with 99% sensitivity, 99% specificity, and 1% disease prevalence, does a positive result mean ~50% or ~99% probability of disease?
side_a: Bayes with base rates ⇒ ~50%; ignoring prevalence is wrong.
side_b: A 99% accurate test means positives are ~99% true positives.

topic: Monty Hall with 3 doors: after the host reveals a goat, is switching doors a 2/3 win strategy or 50/50?
side_a: Switching wins 2/3 — your first pick was wrong with probability 2/3.
side_b: Two doors left ⇒ 50/50 regardless of switching.

topic: Are there infinitely many primes, or could the set be finite?
side_a: Euclid's proof shows any finite list misses a new prime.
side_b: Primes become rare enough that finiteness is plausible.

topic: Should d/dx(x^n)=n·x^(n-1) be justified from the limit definition or accepted as a pattern?
side_a: Derive it from limits + binomial theorem for rigor.
side_b: Pattern matching is enough for applied work.
